The scheduler package itself is a self-contained library (only used in its own tests/README) — there is no actual application code wiring it up to a "database-cleanup" job anywhere else in the repo.

r03. Premise correction: there is no nightly database-cleanup job registered anywhere in this codebase, so no such schedule time exists to report.

What actually exists is `internal/scheduler` (internal/scheduler/scheduler.go, job.go, etc.) — a generic, GitHub-Actions-inspired cron scheduler library. Its own README (`internal/scheduler/README.md:34-35`) and doc comment (`internal/scheduler/doc.go:14-16`) use a hypothetical `"daily-cleanup"` job with `Schedule: "0 2 * * *"` (2 AM) purely as a *usage example*, and its test suite (`internal/scheduler/example_test.go`, `internal/scheduler/integration_test.go`) exercises various cron expressions (`"0 9 * * *"`, `"0 1 * * 0"`, etc.) for demonstration/testing purposes only.

I searched for any real caller of `scheduler.New`/`scheduler.Register` outside the `internal/scheduler` package itself — `find_references` and `grep_content` for `github.com/usememos/memos/internal/scheduler` both came back showing only the package's own README, doc.go, and `*_test.go` files import or invoke it. No production code in the server registers a database-cleanup (or any) job with this scheduler.

So there's no nightly database-cleanup job configured in this repo — the "2 AM" figure you may be thinking of is just illustrative sample code in the scheduler library's own documentation/examples, not a live job.
